merger_description:
Pursuant to the Share Purchase Agreement between Sandvik SRP AB (**Sandvik**), Diemme Filtration S.r.l. (**Diemme**), and Aqseptence Group GmbH (**Seller**), Sandvik intends to acquire 100% of the corporate capital, by way of purchase of a quota from the Seller, of Diemme (the **Acquisition**).

Sandvik, a company incorporated in Sweden, develops, manufactures and sells machinery and systems for the crushing and screening of rock and minerals, primarily serving the mining, infrastructure and construction sectors. Sandvik’s operations form part of a broader mechanical engineering business and encompass product design, production, and global commercialisation, as well as the provision of related aftermarket services and technical support.

Diemme, a company incorporated in Italy, carries on the business of designing, engineering, manufacturing, marketing and installing customised filter presses, filtration and thickening equipment and systems for solid-liquid separation, and the design of equipment for the conversion of waste sludge into biodegradable and organic plastics. Diemme is active in a range of industries, including mining & metals, biofuels, chemicals, and water treatment.

determination_table_content.details:
Sandvik SRP AB (Sandvik) applied for a notification waiver in respect
of its proposed acquisition of 100% of the share capital in Diemme
Filtration S.r.l. (Diemme), as described in the transaction documents
provided as part of the application (the Acquisition).

The Australian Competition and Consumer Commission has
determined under section 51ABV(1)(a) of the Competition and
Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.

The acquirer, Sandvik, is a company incorporated in Sweden which
develops, manufactures and sells machinery and systems for the
crushing and screening of rock and minerals, primarily serving the
mining, infrastructure and construction sectors. Sandvik’s operations
form part of a broader mechanical engineering business and
encompass product design, production, and global
commercialisation, as well as the provision of related aftermarket
services and technical support.
The target, Diemme, is a company incorporated in Italy which
designs, engineers, manufactures, markets and installs customised
filter presses, filtration and thickening equipment and systems for
solid-liquid separation, and which designs equipment for the
conversion of waste sludge into biodegradable and organic plastics.
Diemme is active in a range of industries, including mining & metals,
biofuels, chemicals, and water treatment.
Both parties are active in the supply of mining equipment in
Australia. However, the application states that they supply different
types of equipment which perform distinct functions at different
stages of the mineral processing operation.

In making this notification waiver determination, the Australian
Competition and Consumer Commission (the ACCC) has considered
the information provided with the notification waiver application and
had regard to the factors in section 51ABV(2)(b) of the Competition
and Consumer Act 2010 (Cth) (the Act).
Based on the information currently before it, the ACCC considers that
the Acquisition is unlikely to give rise to any material lessening of
competition. In particular:
a. there is no horizontal overlap or vertical relationship
between Sandvik and Diemme in Australia
b. there are alternative suppliers of the types of mining
equipment supplied by each of the parties in Australia
c. there is a low risk of foreclosure or other concerning
conglomerate effects resulting from exclusionary conduct,
bundling or tying of products and services post-acquisition.
In these circumstances, the ACCC does not consider it necessary to
reach a concluded view on the likelihood of the notification
thresholds being met.
Given that material competition concerns are unlikely to arise, the
ACCC has determined that the Acquisition is not required to be
notified.
The ACCC considers that the determination is consistent with the
object of the Act and the interests of consumers in promoting
competition.
For more information about the ACCC’s approach to considering
notification waiver applications and to assessing competition
effects more generally, see the ACCC’s interim guidance on
notification waivers and merger assessment guidelines.
